gloss: to be utterly dumbfounded; to be completely appalled

definitions.gloss: to be utterly dumbfounded; to be completely appalled
definitions.explanation: An intensified form of {呆|あき}れる, expressing extreme exasperation or disbelief at someone's behavior or a situation.

examples.japanese: もう{呆|あき}れ{返|かえ}ったよ。
あの{発言|はつげん}には{呆|あき}れ{返|かえ}ってしまった。
examples.english: I was utterly appalled by that remark.

examples.japanese: {何度|なんど}{注意|ちゅうい}しても{直|なお}らないので、{周|まわ}りは{呆|あき}れ{返|かえ}っている。
examples.english: No matter how many times he's warned, he doesn't change, so everyone around him is completely exasperated.

notes:
A compound verb formed from {呆|あき}れる (to be amazed/appalled) + {返|かえ}る (to return). The {返|かえ}る suffix intensifies the base verb, giving a sense of being so shocked that one is left speechless or unable to react. Always carries a negative connotation — expressing disgust, exasperation, or disbelief rather than positive surprise.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {呆|あき}れ{返|かえ}って{物|もの}も{言|い}えない: so appalled one can't even speak
- {呆|あき}れ{返|かえ}った{顔|かお}: a look of utter disbelief
- {呆|あき}れ{返|かえ}ってしまう: to end up completely dumbfounded

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {呆|あき}れる: to be amazed, appalled — the base form; less intense
- {唖然|あぜん}とする: to be stunned — focuses on speechlessness from shock
- {開|あき}いた{口|くち}が{塞|ふさ}がらない: to be left open-mouthed — an idiom expressing extreme shock or disbelief

GRAMMAR NOTE:
The ～{返|かえ}る pattern is a productive compound verb suffix meaning "to do something to an extreme degree" or "all the way back." Other examples include {繰|く}り{返|かえ}す (to repeat) and {振|ふ}り{返|かえ}る (to look back).
